ingredients.name: Roasted rice flour
ingredients.notes: dry-roasted on low heat until lightly golden; reserve 1/4 cup for coating

ingredients.name: Freshly grated coconut
ingredients.notes: fresh is best; dried desiccated coconut can substitute

ingredients.name: Kithul treacle or jaggery
ingredients.notes: adjust to desired sweetness; jaggery should be dissolved in a little warm water first

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: coarsely ground; gives the characteristic peppery warmth

ingredients.name: Hot water
ingredients.notes: a tablespoon or two if the mixture is too dry to roll into balls

steps.instruction: Dry-roast the rice flour in a pan over low-medium heat, stirring constantly, until it turns lightly golden and smells nutty -- about 7-10 minutes. Do not let it burn. Reserve about 1/4 cup of the roasted flour in a separate bowl for coating.
In a mixing bowl, combine the remaining roasted rice flour, grated coconut, black pepper, and salt. Mix together.

Gently heat the treacle in a small pan until it warms and becomes pourable. Add the warm treacle to the flour-coconut mixture gradually, stirring and folding until the mixture comes together into a slightly sticky, moldable paste. If too dry to hold together, add a tablespoon of hot water at a time.
When the mixture has cooled enough to handle, take a small portion (about 1 tablespoon) and roll between your palms into a smooth ball. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Roll each ball in the reserved roasted rice flour to coat, giving them a dry, matte exterior. Optionally also roll in toasted sesame seeds for extra aroma.
Arrange on a plate and let cool completely before serving or storing. Serve with Ceylon tea.

source_site: srilankancuisine.org, cross-checked against elanka.com.au, thefoodsnaps.com, rasakama.wordpress.com, infolanka.com, foodcnr.com, and Wikipedia (Aggala)
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources; strong agreement on roasted rice flour, treacle/jaggery sweetener, pepper, and coconut as the four core components
notes: Aggala are one of the simplest and most ancient Sri Lankan sweets -- essentially a no-bake, no-fry snack made from pantry staples. Traditionally made from sun-dried leftover cooked rice that is then roasted and ground into flour; this entry uses the more common modern shortcut of store-bought rice flour dry-roasted in a pan, which produces an almost identical result. The characteristic peppery flavour from black pepper is considered essential and not optional -- it is what distinguishes aggala from other rice flour sweets. Adding fresh grated coconut reduces shelf life to 1-2 days; making them without coconut (or with only a little desiccated coconut) extends shelf life to 1-2 weeks in an airtight container. Can optionally be rolled in roasted sesame seeds instead of or in addition to rice flour coating.
